```{python}
import os
os.chdir(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), ".."))   # analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations -> analysis
os.chdir("..")                                # -> twogroup_experiments/
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "analysis/logistic_laplace_simulations")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 110
import polars as pl
import cs_tables as C
import delta_figure as F
import posterior_figure as PF
import laplacelib as R

SC = "022-laplace"
d = C.declared(C.load(SC))
sig = d.filter(~pl.col("null"))
```

Five logistic-SuSiE arms, all in the Gaussian family $\mathcal{Q}_2$ (see the
[pilot](results.qmd) for the arm definitions). Design: sparse 0/1 columns ($n = 1000$,
$p = 256$, adjacent-column $\phi = 0.8$), $b_0 = -2$, $L^* = 3$ causals at gap 8 (binary
$\phi \approx 0.47$ between causals) or 64 ($\phi \approx 0.05$), fit with $L = 5$. Axis:
expected set size $m$, with $\beta$ calibrated per $m$ to $E[\text{LRT}] = T$ so detectability
is matched and only the shape of each feature's likelihood changes with $m$.

All CS metrics are over **declared** CSs (component $\log \text{BF} \ge 2$). An undeclared
component has $\alpha$ near uniform and a 95% set of ~240 of 256 features, so its coverage is
1 by construction; pooling it in would erase every difference. The ranking of the arms is the
same at every $\log \text{BF}$ cut from 0 to 10.

```{python}
#| label: status
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
n_cells = sig.select("T", "gap", "m").unique().height
reps = sig.group_by("T", "gap", "m", "method").len()["len"]
print(f"{SC}: {n_cells} signal cells x {sig['method'].n_unique()} arms, "
      f"{reps.min()}-{reps.max()} reps per cell; {d.filter(pl.col('null')).select('m').unique().height} null cells.")
```

# PIPs and effect sizes {#sec-posterior}

The credible set metrics above see only the 95% set of each declared component. The same
fits give per-feature PIPs and per-component effect posteriors. PIPs are computed from the
declared components (log BF $\ge 2$), as the CS metrics are: an undeclared component spreads
about $1/p$ over every feature, invisible per feature but adding about 1 to any sum over the 253
nulls. The effect-size rows condition on detection: over declared components whose 95% set
contains a causal, the component's conditional posterior $N(\mu, \sigma^2)$ on that causal is
compared with the true $b$. The last row needs no matching: $\hat b = \sum_l \alpha_l \mu_l$
is the marginal posterior mean, and the error $\|X(\hat b - b)\|/\sqrt{n}$ on the linear
predictor forgives posterior mass moved between correlated columns.

```{python}
#| label: setup-posterior
#| include: false
P = PF.load_posterior(SC)
```

## PIPs {#sec-pip}

```{python}
#| label: fig-pip-delta
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "PIPs, relative to CAVI. Same experiment and layout as the credible set figure. Rows: mean PIP over the 3 causal features, and the sum of PIPs over the 253 null features (the expected number of false inclusions per fit), both from declared components, each as the arm minus CAVI-Q2 on the same replicates. Bands are 95% intervals from resampling replicates jointly for both arms."
F_pip = PF.metric_frame(P, PF.PIP_METRICS, ref="cavi")
PF.draw(F_pip, PF.PIP_METRICS, ref="cavi");
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-pip-absolute
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "PIPs, absolute. Each arm's own mean PIP on the causals and sum of PIPs on the nulls, from declared components, with per-arm 95% intervals from resampling replicates."
PF.draw(PF.metric_frame(P, PF.PIP_METRICS, ref=None), PF.PIP_METRICS, ref=None);
```

## Effect sizes {#sec-effect}

```{python}
#| label: fig-effect-delta
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Effect size posteriors, relative to CAVI. Rows 1 to 3 condition on detection (declared components whose 95% set contains a causal, on that causal): the conditional posterior mean over the true effect, as the ratio of the arm's mean to CAVI-Q2's (log axis); coverage of the 95% conditional posterior interval $\\mu \\pm 1.96\\sigma$ for the true effect, as the arm minus CAVI-Q2; and the conditional posterior sd as a ratio (log axis). Row 4: root mean squared error of the fitted linear predictor $X \\hat b$ against $X b$, as a ratio to CAVI-Q2's (log axis). Bands are 95% intervals from resampling replicates jointly for both arms."
F_eff = PF.metric_frame(P, PF.EFFECT_METRICS, ref="cavi")
PF.draw(F_eff, PF.EFFECT_METRICS, ref="cavi");
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-effect-absolute
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Effect size posteriors, absolute. Conditional posterior mean over the true effect (log axis, dashed line: unbiased), coverage of the 95% conditional posterior interval (dashed line: nominal), conditional posterior sd, and linear predictor RMSE, with per-arm 95% intervals from resampling replicates. The posterior mean sits far above the truth at small design density for every arm: a column with 5 members is close to separation, the prior variance is estimated (capped at 100), and the conditional posterior is wide and right-skewed."
PF.draw(PF.metric_frame(P, PF.EFFECT_METRICS, ref=None), PF.EFFECT_METRICS, ref=None);
```

# Single causal, L = 1 {#sec-ser}

```{python}
#| label: setup-ser
#| include: false
SC_SER = "022-laplace-ser"
ds = C.declared(C.load(SC_SER))
sigs = ds.filter(~pl.col("null"))
```

The same design with one causal column and the single-effect arms ($L = 1$). At $L = 1$
there are no other effects to fold in, so gIBSS-Q2 and CAVI-Q2 run the same update; any
difference between arms is in the single-effect regression itself. Note the declaration
rate at $T = 8$: a lone causal clears $\log \text{BF} \ge 2$ in only about one fit in eight
(the SER log BF pays $\log p \approx 5.5$ nats against an expected LRT of 8), so the $T = 8$
coverage rests on 25 to 30 declared sets per cell and its intervals are wide. In the $L = 5$
grid the three correlated causals pooled their signal and declared at over one set per fit.

```{python}
#| label: status-ser
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
reps = sigs.group_by("T", "m", "method").len()["len"]
print(f"{SC_SER}: {sigs.select('T', 'm').unique().height} signal cells x {sigs['method'].n_unique()} arms, "
      f"{reps.min()}-{reps.max()} reps per cell; {ds.filter(pl.col('null')).select('m').unique().height} null cells.")
```
